calls.body: The Penguins are one of the league’s best for chance quality, but the Avalanche are the best at preventing dangerous shots. We think the Penguins still get theirs.

calls.head: The Avalanche will send Toews and Makar at Crosby
calls.body: At home, the Avalanche keep sending Toews and Makar out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Jared Bednar has been picking a defense pair for the other team’s top line. Tonight the Penguins’ first line is Crosby, Rust and Rakell.

calls.head: In close against from distance
calls.body: The Penguins get in close, but the Avalanche mostly shoot from distance. Pittsburgh is the league’s best for shots from in close, and Colorado is the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Shots from in close tend to be more dangerous, so expect the Penguins to do more of their damage around the net.

COL.head: We gave Colorado a 63% chance, and they delivered.

PIT.head: We gave Pittsburgh only a 37% chance, and it went the way we feared.

surprises.head: Colorado’s kill smothered Pittsburgh’s power play
surprises.body: Colorado has one of the league’s stingiest penalty kills. Even by those standards, this was a dry night: Pittsburgh’s power play created 1.6 expected goals per 60, against their usual 7.3 (about 6.4 against Colorado) and a league average of 7.6. A team strays this far about once every 30 games.

surprises.head: Colorado got the good looks
surprises.body: Pittsburgh usually allows more dangerous shots than most teams. Even by those standards, this was a night of good looks: Colorado’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 9.3% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.2% (about 6.5% against Pittsburgh) and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 35 games.

story.head: Lehkonen scores two as the Avalanche rally from two down
paras: Evgeni Malkin and Bryan Rust scored 29 seconds apart midway through the first to put the Penguins up 2-0. Artturi Lehkonen got the Avalanche on the board 2:04 later. Lehkonen struck again early in the second to tie it 2-2. Artūrs Šilovs stopped Nathan MacKinnon on a penalty shot early in the second. Gabriel Landeskog put the Avs ahead to cap the comeback 3:59 later. T.J. Hughes, undrafted and in his eighth NHL game, scored his first NHL goal, set up by MacKinnon, late in the second to make it 4-2. MacKinnon made it 5-2 on the power play with 4:54 left. MacKinnon finished with four points: a goal and three assists. Martin Nečas finished with three assists.

The Avalanche carried the play, and got the result to match. The Avalanche had five shots in the first period and trailed 2-1, then outshot the Penguins 27-18 the rest of the way. Mackenzie Blackwood settled in after a shaky start for the Avalanche: he gave up two goals on the first eight shots, then stopped the last 24. The Avalanche moved to 5-2-1, and the Penguins fell to 3-4-1.

items.text: Sidney Crosby passed Joe Thornton for seventh on the NHL’s all-time assists list, with 1,110.
Bryan Rust extended his point streak against Colorado to at least seven games.
Nathan MacKinnon extended his point streak against Pittsburgh to six games.
The Penguins have gone winless in four straight on the road.
